thread:
leo: ping — Acme POC just hit a weird combo: intermittent 401s that clear up, then a bunch of 403s for stream calls. Started right after they switched to their org SSO flow.

fatima: hmm timeline + payloads?

leo: customer sent two snippets. First (401): 

leo: ```
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer eyJhb...ephemeral\" -H \"X-Redwood-Org: acme-corp\" https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate | jq
{
  \"error\": \"invalid_token\",
  \"message\": \"token_expired_or_revoked: token expired 2026-02-28T12:34:56Z\",
  \"code\": 401
}
```

trent: ephemeral tokens from SSO will show up like that if the client didn't refresh. Are they using a refresh flow?

leo: customer said their front-end exchanges an id_token for an org token via our /oauth/token endpoint, but sometimes they get a long-lived token copy pasted by a developer during testing. That could explain the inconsistency.

fatima: the 403 stream error?

leo: second snippet (403): 

leo: ```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  \"error\": \"insufficient_scope\",
  \"message\": \"required scope 'inference:stream' not granted\",
  \"code\": 403
}
```

trent: ok so two issues: expired/ephemeral token not refreshed + token without streaming scope. They might be swapping between tokens in env.

sarah: monitor-bot shows a small token error spike at 15:02 UTC then recovery, which fits.

monitor-bot: metrics: acme-poc - token_errors: 29 (last 15m), avg_rps: 4.6, 95p_latency: 190ms.

fatima: remediation checklist to send customer: 1) confirm they are using org-issued tokens (not personal). 2) if using SSO, implement refresh flow and check expires_in before each call. 3) ensure the token has inference:stream if using streaming APIs. 4) avoid copying long-lived tokens into front-end bundles.

leo: copy for security team request about token auditing: 

fatima: \"Redwood logs token lifecycle events (create, rotate, revoke) and records creator metadata, scope, binding (org/project), and last-used timestamps. Tokens can be short-lived via SSO and integrated with KMS for rotation. Audit exports available via tokens API and console.\"

trent: repro I ran: 

trent: ```
# simulate expired ephemeral token
export RW_KEY=eyJhb...expired
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY\" -H \"X-Redwood-Org: acme-corp\" https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/ping | jq
# -> token_expired_or_revoked
# swap to fresh SSO exchange token -> success
```

leo: I also spotted one subtlety: their frontend was setting header `x-redwood-org` (lowercase) in fetch. Our proxy normalizes headers but older SDKs were case-sensitive in a local middleware and dropped the header, causing implicit org mismatch.

fatima: wow ok add that to notes: \"check header casing/middleware that may strip custom headers\".

trent: suggested quick fixes sent to customer: 1) rotate out long-lived test tokens; 2) use backend-for-frontend to keep tokens off client; 3) add retry/refresh logic for SSO tokens; 4) ensure token includes stream scope if needed.

sarah: customer replied: \"we used a dev token during early tests and a browser change removed our custom header, causing some calls to fall back to default org and fail. We've removed test tokens and patched header middleware.\"

monitor-bot: monitoring: starting 20m watch window for acme-poc.

leo: customer swapped token to org-managed service token with scopes [inference:invoke,inference:stream] and moved the exchange to their backend. Asking if switching to org-managed tokens affects billing/quota.

fatima: short answer: no, token type doesn't change pricing. Quotas and billing follow the org/billing account. If they move to a different org with different plan then quotas/pricing could change.

trent: follow-ups: I'll send repro and code snippets (fetch vs backend example) + rdwctl CLI example. Fatima send security blurb to their security contact. Sarah confirm in CRM.

leo: customer reports no more 4xx errors after fixes. dropping notes in ticket and closing swarm. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
